text:
Nazem Kadri is back in Colorado, where he won the Stanley Cup in 2022, and at 36 he's a real contributor rather than a nostalgia act. Fourteen points in 17 games, five goals in his last ten, and a two-goal night against Chicago on Nov. 2 that Reuters said, along with Jaden Schwartz, carried the Avs past the Blackhawks. That same game started with a Kadri turnover that turned into a Chicago 2-on-1 and a 2-0 hole, per Evan Rawal of the Denver Gazette. It was about as complete a Kadri night as you'll find.

The process is solid rather than spectacular. Colorado gets 52% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, and his finishing sits a touch under what his chances deserve, so there's nothing to give back. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a setup man last season, 88th percentile among forwards in passes that lead directly to shots, and Evolving-Hockey had him drawing more penalties than he takes. His minutes have dipped by about two a night lately, which is the thing to watch for a player his age.
headline: Home again, and still useful
